newsitem.title: CHINA: CHINA WARNS SPORTS DOPING COULD MAKE COMEBACK.
newsitem.headline: CHINA WARNS SPORTS DOPING COULD MAKE COMEBACK.

text.p: China caught 10 athletes using banned substances in 1996, Yuan Weimin, deputy minister of the State Physical Culture and Sports Commission, said on Sunday.
Yuan warned that China, rocked by a doping scandal in 1994, could see a resurgence of performance-enhancing drugs if sports authorities relaxed their vigilance.

"The facts show there are still people leaving things to chance and being reckless," the official Xinhua news agency quoted Yuan as saying. "If we relax in our work, there may be a resurgence of the doping problem."
Sports authorities carried out 2,080 doping tests in 1996, up nine percent on the previous year, he said.
The athletes who tested positive for banned substances were lesser-known figures, Yuan said. He did not identify them or their sport and did not say if they had been punished.
The commission planned to conduct 3,500 doping tests in 1997, including more than 2,000 tests at the Chinese National Games in October, he said.
"We will try our best to have a drug-free games," he said.

China was deeply embarrassed when 11 athletes, including seven swimmers, were suspended from competition in 1994 after testing positive for performance-enchancing drugs at the Asian Games in Hiroshima.
Two world champions were among the seven swimmers given two-year suspensions.
China has angrily denied accusations by the West that its team of world record-breaking women distance runners used performance-enhancing drugs.
